title: Method surface reconciler and call metadata preservation for hybrid tool/function invocations
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement:
Customers and internal clients are increasingly mixing two call styles: older 'legacy function' RPC-like payloads produced by on-prem runtimes and newer OpenAI-style 'tools' described via JSON schema and invoked by the chat model. This leads to two recurring problems in production: (1) name collisions and subtle semantic differences between similarly named operations across ecosystems, and (2) loss of call provenance and structured metadata when we translate between shapes (for example, dropped headers, context tags, or routing hints).

Goal:
Implement a reconciler layer in the runtime API that: (a) reconciles equivalent method/tool names and resolves collisions using deterministic rules and configurable mapping tables, and (b) preserves structured call metadata (provenance, routing hints, client-supplied tags) through translation steps so downstream components (auditing, billing, routing) can rely on stable fields. The outcome should make hybrid invocations opaque to end-services: they receive canonicalized call messages and intact metadata irrespective of whether the client used legacy function syntax or OpenAI-style tool calls.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: name-resolution strategy, canonical envelope format, metadata preservation rules, runtime shim that performs translation for in-flight requests, tests, migration tooling to create mapping entries for customer mappings.
- Out of scope: model-level intent translation, changes to public SDK surfaces (we will keep current SDKs stable), billing schema changes beyond adding preserved metadata fields.

Constraints and considerations:
- Backwards compatibility: any mapping must be opt-in per-customer until we validate heuristics; default behavior should be non-breaking.
- Observability: reconciler must emit tracing spans and structured metrics for mapping decisions, collisions, and dropped fields (if any).
- Performance: translation should add minimal latency — target p50 <= 3ms overhead in the fast-path for single-request invocations.
- Security: preserved metadata may contain tenant identifiers or routing tokens; enforce redaction policies and honor KMS/HSM controls.

Proposed design summary:
1) Canonical envelope: introduce a thin canonical envelope schema used internally: {"method_key":string, "signature_schema":string, "payload":json, "provenance":{...}}. We will keep the envelope representation internal and serialize to/from existing shapes as needed.
2) Name reconciliation: maintain a per-tenant name-resolution table + global heuristics. Resolution order: exact tenant mapping -> exact global mapping -> canonicalization heuristics (case/sep normalization) -> ambiguity flag. Ambiguity results in soft-fail mode returning a disambiguation hint to the client unless tenant has opted-in for automatic fallback.
3) Metadata preservation: copy RBAC and routing tags into provenance.headers and attach a small immutable uuid call_id. Redaction is applied according to tenant policy.
4) Compatibility shim module: a runtime plugin that performs detection (legacy vs tool) and converts input to the canonical envelope, emitting a mapping trace. The plugin also converts responses back to the client-visible shape.

Acceptance criteria:
- Edge cases for colliding names are covered by tests and an admin-facing disambiguation response is implemented.
- Translation adds <=3ms median latency overhead in benchmark harness for 99th percentile payloads under typical sequences.
- Call-level metadata fields (call_id, original_method_name, tenant_mapping_source) are present in logs and traces for every translated request.
- e2e tests that show a legacy-function client invoking an operation which a downstream service receives as the canonicalized tool with preserved provenance.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Introducing a canonical envelope increases internal coupling and requires careful migration of consumers of request messages. Mitigation: keep envelope internal, provide adapters for existing consumers, and a migration window.
- Heuristics may mis-map ambiguous names; require opt-in and a mapping UI for customers.

Open questions:
- Should mapping edits be allowed via the Console UI or only via an API/CLI? (PM prefers UI; infra prefers API-first.)
- What retention period should we keep the mapping audit logs? (Default proposal: 90 days.)

Next steps / implementation plan:
- Spike (2d): benchmark overhead for envelope serialization and a simple mapping in the runtime. Owner: Marco Li.
- Implementation (4w): build shim + mapping store + test harness. Owners: Marco, Priya Menon.
- Integration (1w): add tracing/metrics and surface disambiguation hint to SDKs. Owner: Observability team.
- Migration (2w): opt-in rollout for a set of pilot customers and creation of migration docs. Owners: Solutions Eng + PM.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical envelope implemented and used internally for translated invocations
Per-tenant and global mapping tables with deterministic resolution order
Traceable mapping decisions emitted as structured spans/metrics
Median translation overhead <= 3ms in benchmark harness
End-to-end test where legacy function call is received downstream as canonical tool with provenance
tasks: Spike: measure serialization and mapping latency
Design and document canonical envelope schema
Implement mapping store with API (CRUD) and opt-in flags
Runtime shim: detection, translation to envelope, reverse mapping for responses
Add tracing spans and metrics for mapping decisions
Add redaction hooks and KMS checks for preserved metadata
implementation_notes: Prefer protobuf-lite binary encoding for internal envelope on hot path; fall back to compact JSON only for debug/trace mode. Mapping store will be implemented as a namespaced Redis hash backed by a durable metadata service for edit history. Provide a feature flag to toggle automatic fallback for ambiguous mappings per tenant.
test_plan: Unit tests for normalization heuristics, mapping store CRUD tests, property tests for collision resolution, integration harness with sample legacy and OpenAI-style payloads, latency benchmarks at different QPS and sequence lengths. Include audit log verification tests for provenance fields.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal canaries and infra team exercises (1 week)
Beta: two pilot customers with opt-in mapping tables (2 weeks)
GA: default-on for new tenants; existing tenants remain opt-in for 30 days before automatic migration is offered
